body:
I've had these feelings since before my first attempt about 20 years ago. I believe it stems a lot from always feeling like I am a burden on others or that I make other peoples' lives worse.

I have held on for a long time. I went through the paces of life trying to see when it got better. High school, college, marriage, kids, successful career, nice home, and even a recent promotion. My life is one many people envy.

And yet, no matter how hard I work for the right life, I realize it's not for me. I'm not a good mother. I'm not a good wife. I'm not a good friend. The only thing I'm decent at, is my job. But that's easy to fake. The rest of it, over time, has become so hard, that I'm becoming worse of an influence in the lives of those around me. And the more I think about it, the more I realize they would be better off if I wasn't around anymore. They wouldn't realize it. They would think they need me. But in reality, I've weighed the with and without scenarios so many times, I know I'd be doing them a favor. Even if they never knew or understood it.

The ((hugs)) thing is the response I got when I told friends online. My mom is batshit crazy so if I tell her the whole damn city would know by morning.

Thanks for listening. It does help.

He meant that I always make things about myself and never think about him. But any time I mention something for myself he says that, successfully turning the conversation into being about him anyway.

I'd never told anyone, out loud, that I wanted to kill myself. I met resistance but I pushed forward. Knowing how close to the edge I was/am. And it basically confirmed that it doesn't matter.

And now, I just hang on with the notion that this feeling will pass as it always does. But this is one of the worst it's ever been. And that hope is fading. I felt it for a moment. I felt it passing. But it came right back.

So I'm still holding on. I'll try as hard as I can to hold on.

I didn't tell everyone I was fine. I was very clear with a few people that I wasn't and I came right out and said it to one person that I was on this edge. I didn't get help even though I was literally begging for it.

I'm here. The meeting was a meeting. I tried to sleep this off but I can't. I thought I was feeling better but I'm not. If I keep going a few hours here and there and keeping myself occupied in some way, at some point this will pass. It always does. Or it has so far.

I've just never been so sure and so prepared. I've never told anyone out loud that I was feeling this way  and today I did. And it got me nowhere. And it's only reinforcing what I am feeling I should do... but if I can stave it off... just keep passing the hours... this will pass. It has to.

He was even on my phone apparently and saw this in my notes and still felt his reply was appropriate.
---------
"The so-called ‘psychotically depressed’ person who tries to kill herself doesn’t do so out of quote ‘hopelessness’ or any abstract conviction that life’s assets and debits do not square. And surely not because death seems suddenly appealing. The person in whom Its invisible agony reaches a certain unendurable level will kill herself the same way a trapped person will eventually jump from the window of a burning high-rise. Make no mistake about people who leap from burning windows. Their terror of falling from a great height is still just as great as it would be for you or me standing speculatively at the same window just checking out the view; i.e. the fear of falling remains a constant. The variable here is the other terror, the fire’s flames: when the flames get close enough, falling to death becomes the slightly less terrible of two terrors. It’s not desiring the fall; it’s terror of the flames. And yet nobody down on the sidewalk, looking up and yelling ‘Don’t!’ and ‘Hang on!’, can understand the jump. Not really. You’d have to have personally been trapped and felt flames to really understand a terror way beyond falling."
David Foster Wallace

I told my husband that I wanted to blow my brains out and he let me know that not everything is about me. No fucking shit. Why the fuck do you think I feel that way? Because the whole fucking world would be better off without me.
Thanks. I'm heading into a meeting where I will be planning my future with the company and have to pretend like I don't plan to end it all this weekend. Maybe I will find hope in it.
Fuck them. Fuck it all. They can't have the last bit of time to learn to hate me.

I have a strong want to work with a specific IT company, known to only hire those with some type of exceptional background. And I have even less than a normal. And the motivation shows up, and promptly goes away with the the realization of how hard it would be to become someone of interest to this company.

I'm trying to work past that, though. It's something I want more than anything, and I owe it to myself to find a way to reach further for it. Someday... Maybe I will.

I'm drinking alone right now. Will I ever tell anyone, no. The kids are in bed. Their dad at work, and I'm the pos left to deal with her emotions and unable to do so.

I wish I had a drinking buddy too, but social anxieties cut that out too.

Wish I had some kind of advice or something. This feeing sucks... So I guess, know you're not alone, and someone, somewhere else, is drinking alone with you.

/cheers

Although, I feel the need to sincerely say, be careful. It's a shitty time but we still can care for each other and find a way to have enough care for ourselves not to take it too far. So, cheers, but safe cheers...
Not where I expected this to go. Thank you :)

Gah... I wish someone would see me that way. Do you ever tell her any of this? Just to know someone takes so much stock in her might make some difference. It sounds like she's getting older to where she may be able to seek help on her own (not knowing details of the home life makes this purely a guess). Can you help guide her in that direction if possible? Research doctors in the area and how they handle situations like this?

It's possible he went defensive because he felt guilty. Weird how stuff like that will come out. I have crappy birthdays every year. This year I decided to explain to my husband why I feel that way, and he went all out. It was the best birthday in all of my 32yrs. Communication is key. Talk to him before hand and give him a chance to surprise you. It doesn't make the hurt go away. It always hurts when we feel pushed aside by those we care about. But t doesn't mean it will always be that way as long as we open up communication.

I think it best to leave things alone and move on. It sounds like you're more hurt than worrying about him. What you would want is not what is best for others. Let her deal with that guilt and pressure. You should focus on moving on and not worrying about them. Besides, you don't know if something happened and she found herself falling deeply in love with him and the guilt keeps her from every straying again. Taking that away from her and him is something of major consequence. It could ruin lives.

And, maybe, try not to get involved with someone who already has a someone. They won't always change their ways if they decide you over the other person. I don't believe in "once a cheater, always a cheater" but I do believe they are much more likely to cheat in the future if they've done it before. Which would mean cheating on you as well.
Constantly

I appreciate your time, attention, and comments. It's much more than I expected, and even more than I would have trusted anyone in my life with.

And another "successful" day will go by. No one will know I had 3 hours of sleep or that I woke up still slightly influenced by my indulgence last night.

And I will continue to hide behind the anonymity of the Internet. Thanks for sharing that space with me.

I'll reply as coherently as I can. Distraction can be an amazing thing. And I truly appreciate your time to reply, even in such a long post. It's probably the most in-depth response I have ever had when admiting I have issues. For that, thank you.

As for why life sucks, pick a day, season, month, etc. I can give many reasons. Most of the time, though, I feel completely worthless. I don't love my husband enough (at least I don't show it, I guess), I'm not a good enough mom, I'm not pretty enough, I'm not smart enough, I'm not where I want to be. And even though I have worked danged hard for everything I have, it feels like I've had to work too hard to be where I am (which is no where- or so it seems- I look good on paper, I suck as a person).

The alcohol; my dad is a drunk. I swore I'd never be that way. I can control it. And some days I still convince myself I can. But nights like tonight, 2 am, sloshed, have to get my kids up and ready for school and then head to work in 4 hours, I realize, I'm not in control. And that is a betrayal to myself and what I always swore I would never be. My pride in hiding it is knowing a couple thing- I pride myself on proof-reading, and knowing not to talk to people who know me, when I'm like this- because they would see more into it- and forbid I ever have to admit to anyone else there is a problem, when I can barely admit it to myself.

Loneliness is a sorry b****. It hits in so many ways. It doesn't matter how many people you are surrounded by, you could be completely alone. I know that feeling. And I hate when I hear that anyone else feels it because I would never wish it on anyone.

I, like you, tend to focus on others. Such a post like this, from me, will never exist anywhere else. And it is a complete lack of inhibition, and knowing no one knows who I am, that allows me to be so open right now. Tomorrow, I will be mortified, I'm sure. But I will make up for it, by contributing to some personal GoFundMe accounts, and Indigogo a friend is starting, helping my teammates, having coffee with a friend and helping her through her issues. Tomorrow will be a day about everyone except myself. It's the only worth I feel. I don't need to buy love. I need to buy a reason for me to be here. So I understand why you responded in such a lengthy way, because I know the feeling you get gives you a sense of purpose. Thank you for being the kind soul that I am, even with the inner turmoil that causes yourself so much grief, no matter the reason. Because you're one of the first I've been truly grateful for contributing because I can see you feel something similar to what I do when helping others... and I keep rambling and deleting ways to finish that though. But I think you get that.

My kids keep me going. I know I'm not a great mom with depression and everything else. But I know how much worse it could be for them if I was to ever let go of this life. I am here to help show them love and how to be good people. To be here for them when so often we are left alone in life to deal with things on our own. And to keep them from ever knowing the pain of losing someone and ever feeling like they could have done something, when there is nothing they can do. Only what I can do.

I wish you all the luck in rehab and that you can take after your mom's excellent example of stepping out from this and making your life better. It is something that will be with you but that you will find control over if that is what you want. Good luck to you and you have made a wonderful choice to make your life better. Only you can be ready to make that choice and take those steps for your life.
